name: Cardinalidae
description: Cardinalidae is a family of New World passerine birds comprising cardinals, grosbeaks, buntings, and the tanagers of the genera Piranga, Habia, and Chlorothraupis, which were moved here from Thraupidae following molecular phylogenetic studies.

children.name: Cardinalis
children.description: The true cardinals — crested, thick-billed passerines named for the brilliant red plumage of the male, which resembles the robes of Catholic cardinals. They are among the most recognisable and popular birds in the Americas, with a rich vocabulary of whistled songs.

children.name: Cardinalis cardinalis
children.description: The northern cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis), also commonly known as the common cardinal, red cardinal, or simply cardinal, is a bird in the genus Cardinalis.

children.name: Cardinalis sinuatus
children.description: The pyrrhuloxia or desert cardinal (Cardinalis sinuatus) is a medium-sized North American songbird found in the American southwest and northern Mexico. This distinctive species with a short, stout bill, red crest, and red wings closely resembles the northern cardinal and the vermilion cardinal, which are in the same genus.

children.name: Cardinalis phoeniceus
children.description: The vermilion cardinal (Cardinalis phoeniceus) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.

children.name: Pseudocyanocompsa viridis
children.description: The Green-crowned Quail is a medium-sized bird with a distinctive green crown and white throat patch. Found in shrublands and woodland edges, it feeds on seeds and fruits. Males have a bright red breast.

children.name: Granatellus caerulescens
children.description: The Blue-throated Granate is a small bird with a bright blue throat patch and reddish-brown plumage. It inhabits open savannas and grasslands, where it feeds on insects and seeds. Males sing complex songs during breeding.

children.name: Pheucticus
children.description: New World grosbeaks with massive conical bills adapted for cracking hard seeds and nuts. Males are boldly patterned in black, white, and bright yellow or rose-red.

children.name: Pheucticus ludovicianus
children.description:
The rose-breasted grosbeak (Pheucticus ludovicianus), colloquially called "cut-throat" due to its coloration, is a large, seed-eating grosbeak in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). It is primarily a foliage gleaner. Males have black heads, wings, backs, and tails, and a bright rose colored patch on their white breast. Males and females exhibit marked sexual dimorphism.
Breeding habitat consists of cool-temperate open deciduous woods throughout much of eastern North America, with migration to tropical America in winter. Rose-breasted grosbeaks have an average maximum lifespan of 7.3 years in the wild, and up to 24 years in captivity. Death in the wild is generally due to collision with objects (buildings, cars, etc.) and predation, to eggs, nestlings and adults.

children.name: Pheucticus melanocephalus
children.description:
The black-headed grosbeak (Pheucticus melanocephalus) is a medium-sized, seed-eating bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is sometimes considered conspecific with the rose-breasted grosbeak (P. Ludovicianus) with which it hybridizes on the American Great Plains.
The long, black-headed grosbeak is a migratory bird, with nesting grounds from southwestern British Columbia, through the western half of the United States, into central Mexico. It occurs as a vagrant further south in Central America.

children.name: Pheucticus chrysogaster
children.description: The golden grosbeak (Pheucticus chrysogaster), also known as golden-bellied grosbeak or southern yellow grosbeak, is a species of grosbeak in the family Cardinalidae.

children.name: Pheucticus aureoventris
children.description: The black-backed grosbeak (Pheucticus aureoventris) is a bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, and Venezuela. They are often kept as cagebirds.

children.name: Pheucticus chrysopeplus
children.description: The yellow grosbeak (Pheucticus chrysopeplus), also known as the Mexican yellow grosbeak, is a medium-sized seed-eating bird in the same family as the northern cardinal, "tropical" or "New World" buntings, and "cardinal-grosbeaks" or New World grosbeaks.

children.name: Pheucticus tibialis
children.description:
The black-thighed grosbeak (Pheucticus tibialis) is a large seed-eating bird in the family Cardinalidae, which is endemic to the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama.
This species breeds from about altitude (Pacific slope) or (Caribbean slope) up to and is found in canopy, woodland edge and semi-open habitats such as pasture with some trees. The nest is a thin cup constructed on a bulky twig base up in a small tree or amongst vines. The female lays two brown-spotted pale blue eggs between March and May.

children.name: Passerina
children.description: New World buntings — small, brilliantly coloured seed-eating birds with vivid blues, indigos, and greens in the males. Young males take two years to attain full adult plumage.

children.name: Passerina caerulea
children.description: The blue grosbeak (Passerina caerulea) is a medium-sized North American passerine bird in the cardinal family Cardinalidae.

children.name: Passerina cyanea
children.description: The indigo bunting (Passerina cyanea) is a small seed-eating bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae.

children.name: Passerina amoena
children.description: The lazuli bunting (Passerina amoena) is a North American songbird named for the gemstone lapis lazuli.

children.name: Passerina ciris
children.description: The painted bunting (Passerina ciris) is a species of bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae.

children.name: Passerina rositae
children.description: The rose-bellied bunting or Rosita's bunting (Passerina rositae) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is endemic to a very small area of southern Mexico.

children.name: Passerina leclancherii
children.description: The orange-breasted bunting (Passerina leclancherii) is a species of passerine bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is endemic to Mexico, where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland. With its wide range and large total population, the International Union for Conservation of Nature considers it as being of "least concern".

children.name: Passerina versicolor
children.description: The varied bunting (Passerina versicolor) is a species of songbird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae.

children.name: Spiza
children.description: A monotypic genus of grassland bird named for its distinctive song — a dry, buzzing 'dick-dick-cissel'. It is locally common but notably irruptive.

children.name: Spiza americana
children.description: The dickcissel (Spiza americana) is a small seed-eating migratory bird in the family Cardinalidae. It breeds on the prairie grasslands of the Midwestern United States and winters in Central America, northern Colombia, and northern Venezuela. It is the only member of the genus Spiza, though some sources list another supposedly extinct species.

children.name: Cyanocompsa
children.description: A genus of predominantly blue seedeaters and grosbeaks found in the Neotropics. Males are deep ultramarine blue; females are warm brown.

children.name: Cyanocompsa parellina
children.description: The blue bunting (Cyanocompsa parellina) is a species of passerine in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks.

children.name: Cyanocompsa brissonii

children.name: Caryothraustes
children.description: A small genus of robust, thick-billed grosbeaks found in lowland forests of Central and South America. They are highly social, often foraging in noisy flocks in the canopy.

children.name: Caryothraustes canadensis
children.description: The yellow-green grosbeak (Caryothraustes canadensis) is a species of grosbeak in the family Cardinalidae.

children.name: Caryothraustes poliogaster
children.description: The black-faced grosbeak (Caryothraustes poliogaster) is a large seed-eating bird in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae), which is a resident breeding species from south-eastern Mexico to eastern Panama.

children.name: Caryothraustes erythromelas
children.description: Caryothraustes erythromelas (Red-and-black Grosbeak) is a cardinalidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Periporphyrus
children.description: A monotypic or small genus of Neotropical grosbeaks with a massive, brightly coloured bill. Found in lowland forests of the Guianas and Amazon.

children.name: Periporphyrus erythromelas
children.description: The red-and-black grosbeak (Periporphyrus erythromelas) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found in Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela.

children.name: Periporphyrus celaeno
children.description: Periporphyrus celaeno (Crimson-collared Grosbeak) is a cardinalidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Amaurospiza
children.description: A genus of secretive, predominantly blue seedeaters found in dense undergrowth in Central and South American forests. They are difficult to observe and remain poorly known.

children.name: Amaurospiza concolor
children.description: The blue seedeater (Amaurospiza concolor) or Cabanis's seedeater is a species of bird in the cardinal family that is found in southern Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Amaurospiza moesta

children.name: Amaurospiza aequatorialis

children.name: Amaurospiza relicta

children.name: Chlorothraupis
children.description: Medium-sized, olive-and-yellow tanagers formerly placed in Thraupidae but now assigned to Cardinalidae on molecular evidence. They inhabit lowland and foothill forest understorey in Central and South America.

children.name: Chlorothraupis carmioli
children.description: Carmiol's tanager (Chlorothraupis carmioli) is a species of bird in the cardinal family Cardinalidae that is found in Central America from Nicaragua southwards to northwest Colombia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest. It was formerly considered as conspecific with the yellow-lored tanager.

children.name: Chlorothraupis olivacea
children.description: The lemon-spectacled tanager (Chlorothraupis olivacea) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, subtropical or tropical moist montane forest, and heavily degraded former forest.

children.name: Chlorothraupis stolzmanni
children.description: The ochre-breasted tanager (Chlorothraupis stolzmanni) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. As a fairly common species with a stable population, the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated this bird as being of "least concern".

children.name: Chlorothraupis monticola
children.description: The Mountain Emerald is a small bird with bright green plumage and white throat patch. It inhabits mountain forests and shrublands, where it feeds on insects and seeds. Males sing complex songs during breeding.

children.name: Chlorothraupis frenata
children.description: Chlorothraupis frenata (Olive Tanager) is a tanagers species found in its native region.

children.name: Piranga
children.description: A genus of brightly coloured tanagers formerly placed in Thraupidae but now assigned to Cardinalidae on molecular evidence. Males are typically vivid red, orange, or yellow; females are duller.

children.name: Piranga flava
children.description: The red tanager (Piranga flava) is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae.

children.name: Piranga bidentata
children.description: The flame-colored tanager (Piranga bidentata), formerly known as the stripe-backed tanager, is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found from Mexico throughout Central America to northern Panama and occasionally in the United States; four subspecies are recognized. The flame-colored tanager is long, the male having predominantly red-orange while the female is more yellowish orange.

children.name: Piranga leucoptera
children.description: The white-winged tanager (Piranga leucoptera) is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found from Mexico, through Central America, across northern South America and as far south as Bolivia.

children.name: Piranga erythrocephala
children.description: The red-headed tanager (Piranga erythrocephala) is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks, endemic to Mexico. Comprising two subspecies, it is around long. Males have predominantly yellow-olive plumage with a red head and throat and females have yellow forecrowns.

children.name: Piranga rubriceps
children.description: The red-hooded tanager (Piranga rubriceps), is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Piranga rubra

children.name: Piranga roseogularis
children.description: The rose-throated tanager (Piranga roseogularis) is a medium-sized songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. Endemic to the Yucatán Peninsula in Central America, it is found in Belize, Guatemala, and Mexico. The male has greyish plumage with a deep rose throat and crown, while the female is similar but for a yellow crown and throat.

children.name: Habia
children.description: Medium-sized, dark-plumaged tanagers formerly placed in Thraupidae but now assigned to Cardinalidae. They are associated with dense undergrowth and often follow army ant swarms.

children.name: Habia rubica
children.description: The red-crowned ant tanager (Habia rubica) is a medium-sized passerine bird from tropical America. It is the only species now placed in the genus Habia. This species was long placed with the tanagers (Thraupidae), but it is actually closer to the cardinals (Cardinalidae).

children.name: Habia fuscicauda
children.description:
The red-throated ant tanager (Driophlox fuscicauda) is a medium-sized passerine bird. This species is a resident breeder on the Caribbean slopes from southeastern Mexico to eastern Panama. It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia. It was usually considered an aberrant kind of tanager and placed in the Thraupidae, but is actually closer to the cardinals (Cardinalidae). Consequently, it can be argued that referring to the members of this genus as ant tanagers is misleading, but no other common name has gained usage.
Red-throated ant tanagers are long and weigh. Adult males are dull dusky red, somewhat paler below, and with a bright red throat and central crown. The female is brownish olive, paler and greyer below, and with a yellow throat and small dull yellow crown stripe. Young birds are brown and lack the throat and crown patches.

children.name: Habia atrimaxillaris
children.description: The black-cheeked ant tanager (Driophlox atrimaxillaris) is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is endemic to Costa Rica. It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia.

children.name: Habia gutturalis
children.description:
The sooty ant tanager (Driophlox gutturalis) is a species of bird in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). It was formerly placed with the true tanagers in the family Thraupidae and was assigned to the genus Habia with the red-crowned ant tanager.
It is endemic to Colombia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and secondary forest. It is becoming rare due to habitat loss.

children.name: Habia cristata
children.description: The crested ant tanager (Driophlox cristata) is a bird in the family Cardinalidae that is endemic to Colombia. It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia.

children.description: The glaucous-blue grosbeak (Cyanoloxia glaucocaerulea), also known as the indigo grosbeak, is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found in Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay.
